name: FlareModel sources
description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window: FlareWorkspace (document, selection, tool, frame and playback, drafts) and FlareServices: the use-case contracts, their live conformances over FlareCore (LiveStage, LiveHits, LiveShapes, LiveProperties, LiveKeyframes, LiveEasing, LiveScenes, and LiveExportAdapter, FlareCore's SVG, Lottie and PNG exporters over any stage: text removed first, a cancel between PNG frames writes nothing, every result carries ExportScan's warnings), and the fixture fakes the UI track and snapshots run on. FlareLaunch parses the launch flags (-FlareFixture, -FlareSample, -FlareOpenFile, -FlareSaveTo) into the workspace's first document and services, and FlareServicesBuilt is FlareServices.built, the live type for every member whose live conformance has merged, which a launch without -FlareFixture runs on. FlareIntent names every control of the window as one case per area with a stable identifier, and FlareIntent+Titles gives each its menu or toolbar title. FlareStageRead gives the stage its draw list (the drag preview while a move runs) and marks (draft, marquee, selection bounds); FlareTimelineRead gives the timeline its rows, empty text and selected row; FlarePenFinish ends an open pen path on Return as one step. FlareWorkspaceState holds the export, assist and file-load states the workspace stores. FlareFiles opens .flare files through load (progress first, a pure decode the app runs off the main thread, then the landing), hands the app a save's bytes, and keeps the file name, the window title and the dirty flag (the document against the one last opened or saved), with section 3.3's alert text for each FormatError, the Open Recent list (file paths, most recent first, at most ten), and the autosave due time (30 seconds after the last edit, only while dirty) with the recovery bytes of the dirty document, and restoring a recovered document as unsaved, untitled work. FlareSelection picks layers or items by click, Shift-click and marquee, and gives the selection box's bounds; FlareDrag turns stage gestures into a draft or move preview and commits each once, on mouse-up, as one named undo step; FlareLiveDrag runs a drag's samples on a copy of the workspace the window doesn't observe, for the stage to draw until mouse-up hands the window the last one; FlareDrawing adds the Ellipse tool's draft and its one-step commit; FlareScenes adds, renames, removes (never the last), reorders and sets up scenes; FlareGuides adds, moves (one coalesced step per drag), removes and clears ruler guides; FlareEdit runs the Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Select All, Deselect), each one named undo step or disabled with the reason it refuses with; FlareAnimate holds auto-key and the inspector's animated properties (Mixed across layers, one coalesced step per scrub, the stopwatch and keyframe button); EasingEditing is the easing editor's contract, which FlareWorkspace conforms to over FlareCore's SetKeyframeEasing, with FakeEasingEditing as its in-memory stand-in for UI work. FlareOnionState holds onion skin and motion path preferences and reads ghosts and the path from services.onion. FlareServices holds one fake per use-case contract (FakeScenes, FakeStage, FakeHits, FakeShapes, FakeProperties with section 2's not-animated rule, FakeKeyframes, FakeEasing, FakeOnion, FakeLibrary, FakeMachines, FakePreview and FakeExport with FakeRasterizer so far, NotBuilt for the rest) over the fixture documents in FlareFixtures (empty, bounce, character, button, button with states, button with machine and showcase). ExportScan names everything an export can't write (text, symbol animation, machines, Lottie's background); FlareExport holds the export sheet's options, warnings and run. FlareSymbols holds the Library tab's symbols and swatches, Convert to Symbol, place, the reason Delete is disabled while a symbol is in use, and editing a symbol in place: the owner switch, the symbol's length on the timeline and the scene frame to return to. FlarePlaybackTicks is the playback driver's platform-neutral core: PlaybackTicker turns display-link target timestamps into the elapsed seconds the play clock advances by, FlareWorkspace.tick is the link's entry point, and PlaybackBudget holds QB-L4's dropped-frame gate. MachineLayout lays out a state machine's graph for the Interactions editor: columns by breadth-first distance from the initial state, unreachable states in a last column. FlareMachines holds the Interactions editor's state: the edited machine, states from frame labels, transitions and inputs, each edit one named undo step through services.machines with refusals in machineError, and the live preview over services.preview, which any machine edit stops.
